title: 2012 HMMT February Guts Problem 7
statement: \(M\) is an \(8 \times 8\) matrix. For \(1 \leq i \leq 8\), all entries in row \(i\) are at least \(i\), and all entries on column \(i\) are at least \(i\). What is the minimum possible sum of the entries of \(M\) ?

solutions.text: 372 Let \(s_{n}\) be the minimum possible sum for an \(n\) by \(n\) matrix. Then, we note that increasing it by adding row \(n+1\) and column \(n+1\) gives \(2 n+1\) additional entries, each of which has minimal size at least \(n+1\). Consequently, we obtain \(s_{n+1}=s_{n}+(2 n+1)(n+1)=s_{n}+2 n^{2}+3 n+1\). Since \(s_{0}=0\), we get that \(s_{8}=2\left(7^{2}+\ldots+0^{2}\right)+3(7+\ldots+0)+8=372\).
